Definition: from (a presumed derivative of) G1085; a generation; by implication, an age (the period or the persons):--age, generation, nation, time.
BiblicalUsage: The plain sense of geneá is age, generation, nation, time. It comes up 37 times, and the passages from Matthew, Mark, Luke, and Acts show how steadily Scripture uses it. I do not find a second, secret meaning hiding behind it.
TheologicalSignificance: geneá matters to me because God works through generations, and no generation is forgotten by Him. I read this as a reminder that God’s words mean what they say, and I can trust them.
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; Mary Visits Elizabeth; Pentecost
